title: Lübeck, from the Lübeck/Hamburg plate in Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1
notes: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1 (Köln, 1593), shelfmark A 330 A Folio RES::1-2, DOI 10.11588/diglit.12704, CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Lübeck and Hamburg share ONE engraved sheet (page 24a), so this row and its twin cite the same object. The plate was viewed, not just catalogued. The Lübeck cartouche reads 'LVBECA VRBS IMPERIALIS LIBERA, CIVITATVM WANDALICARVM ET INCLYTAE HANSEATICAE SOCIETATIS CAPVT' - a contemporary witness naming the city head of the Hanseatic societas, which is an essay claim in its own right and should get an evidence row.

title: Bruges, from Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1
notes: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1 (Köln, 1593), shelfmark A 330 A Folio RES::1-2, DOI 10.11588/diglit.12704, CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Bird's-eye plan; the cartouche reads 'BRVGAE, FLANDRICARVM VRBIVM ORNAMENTA'. The plate was viewed. It witnesses the Kontor's urban setting; whether the Hanseatic house itself is identifiable on it has NOT been established and must not be assumed. TRANSCRIBED from the lower-left text block, closing line: 'Optimam urbium formam, hoc est, orbicularem, situ obtinet, aquis probe instructa, duplici fossa ambitur; florentissimum quondam emporium fuit.' Note the tense: by 1593 the plate describes Bruges as having ONCE BEEN a most flourishing emporium.

title: Köln, from Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1
notes: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1 (Köln, 1593), shelfmark A 330 A Folio RES::1-2, DOI 10.11588/diglit.12704, CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Bird's-eye plan on the Rhine, banner 'COLONIA AGRIPPINA', with the imperial eagle and the city arms. The plate was viewed. Köln is a Rhenish Hanseatic city and a KAN-306 core place; three descriptive text blocks on the plate have not been transcribed. TRANSCRIBED from the lower-right text block: 'Primum in publico Imperij conventu inter vrbes locum obtinet. In peraugusto et celebri Hanseatico foedere septuaginta duarum civitatum, inter quatuor praecipuas recensetur.' - it holds first place among cities in the Empire's public assembly, and in the most august and famous Hanseatic league OF SEVENTY-TWO CITIES it is reckoned among the FOUR PRINCIPAL ones. Two citable figures. No evidence row yet: Köln has no feature in places.csv, so this waits on KAN-306.

title: Bremen, from the four-city plate in Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1
notes: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1 (Köln, 1593), shelfmark A 330 A Folio RES::1-2, DOI 10.11588/diglit.12704, CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Bremen is the lower-left prospect, captioned 'BREMA', a river view with shipping on the Weser. The sheet carries FOUR cities: Braunschweig, Lüneburg, Bremen and Oldenburg, so a citation must name the panel, not just the page. The plate was viewed. Note for KAN-308: the Lüneburg panel above is captioned 'LVNEBVRGVM, NOBILIS SAXONIAE VRBS, SALINIS CELEBERRIMA' - most famous for its salt - which bears on the salt commodity argument.
